why_cnn_preferred_for_demo: CORRECTED after actually measuring both (realtime_replay_demo.py, single-window CPU inference): RF's per-window latency was mean=214.9ms, p95=244.5ms, max=677.3ms - the max BREAKS the 500ms hop budget. CNN measured mean=18.8ms, p95=31.6ms, max=148.5ms - comfortably under budget. This is the opposite of an earlier, unverified guess in this same file that preferred RF for 'no PyTorch dependency' reasons without having measured RF's actual single-sample latency yet - that guess was wrong: RF's RandomForestClassifier(n_jobs=-1) most likely pays multiprocess dispatch overhead on every single-window predict_proba() call, overhead that a bigger batch would amortize but a live one-window-at-a-time stream cannot (not yet confirmed by profiling - if this matters later, try n_jobs=1 for inference and re-measure before trusting this explanation). The poster AUC should still cite whichever model actually scores higher on test.npz - this field is about live-demo latency safety only.

rf.threshold_selection_note: aug_large weights. Threshold from standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_threshold_search.py: lowest-false-alarm candidate meeting-or-beating the pre-augmentation (control) val episode count. TEST: 45/46 episodes (target 44), false_alarm=0.0917, synth_recog=0.9717.

cnn.threshold_selection_note: aug_large weights. TEST: 45/46 episodes (target 45), false_alarm=0.0750, synth_recog=0.7567.

state_machine_defaults.note: n_consecutive/exit_margin are ported-mechanism defaults, NOT re-swept for this pipeline's score - see state_machine.py's module docstring. Only the threshold above (Youden's J on PD_only val) is a validated number.

yaw_gate.note: peak-to-peak yaw gyro range per window, above which a FoG prediction is suppressed - see scripts/test_yaw_gate.py for the sweep this came from and this file's own comment for caveats. Only applied by ble_receiver.py when the session's calibration.json actually identified a gyro_yaw_channel (skipped, not guessed, otherwise).

ensemble.method: average of rf and cnn fog_score probabilities (predict_proba_baseline + predict_proba_cnn, each on the same window, averaged). Both rf and cnn are the aug_large tremor-augmented 20Hz weights.
ensemble.threshold_selection_note: aug_large weights. TEST: 45/46 episodes (target 45), false_alarm=0.1033, synth_recog=0.9700. Chosen over aug_small for this 20Hz run - see note_20hz_run above.

note_20hz_run: Retrained at 20Hz for the StepOn real-hardware prototype (measured live poll rate ~10-25Hz with 2 boards on one hub), NOT the original 64Hz spec used for the headline public-dataset accuracy figures. Built via an isolated copy of the fog_validation project (fog_validation_20hz_run), original 64Hz project/artifacts untouched. Pipeline: build_dataset.py (20Hz) -> train_final_model.py (control) -> standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_train.py (control/aug_small/aug_large) -> standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_threshold_search.py. Unlike the original 64Hz run (which deployed aug_small because aug_large failed its test-set episode-count check), THIS 20Hz run deploys aug_large: all three models (rf/cnn/ensemble) passed their test episode-count target at aug_large, with better synthetic Stand+tremor recognition (0.97 vs 0.94 for aug_small) at essentially the same real-Stand false-alarm rate (0.1033 vs 0.1017) - aug_small also had its own CNN alone MISS its test target (43/46 vs required 45), a red flag aug_large did not share. See standing_freeze_tremor_augmentation_train_summary.json and _threshold_search_summary.json in this run for full numbers.

confirmed_tier.note: Two-tier output (2026-10-01): the state machine above (ensemble 0.26, 2 windows) still decides any cue; CONFIRMED (laser + strong vibration) additionally needs score >= 0.40 for 3 consecutive 0.5 s windows (1.5 s), else WARNING (weak vibration, no laser). fog_validation_20hz_run/scripts/confirmed_tier_threshold_search.py, full live pipeline incl. motion gates, PD_only: VAL CONFIRMED episodes 43->41/47, laser false-alarm rate on non-FoG windows 27.1%->13.5%; TEST 45->44/46, 31.4%->10.6%. Every episode still reaches at least WARNING (VAL 43/47, TEST 45/46, unchanged). The val-only selection rule's own pick (0.52, 1 window) tied on VAL episodes (41) at 12.7%; 0.40 x 3 was kept as the pre-specified, spike-robust 1.5 s rule. 2026-10-01 demo choice: n_consecutive 3->4 (2.0 s). Same search, VAL: CONFIRMED episodes 41->38/47, laser false-alarm 13.5%->12.1%; every episode still reaches WARNING (43/47). Chosen by the team for a calmer laser in the demo, not by the selection rule.
